solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Without failing, riotous raids take to the sky

indicators.note: raiders break into a place, so one word's letters go inside another's

parts.note: to take to the sky is to fly
a riotous mob is out of control, without law

explanation.surface: Rioters' raids succeed every time, and the attackers fly off afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raids' looks like a noun that rioters make, but it is a verb: the riotous word breaks into the flying word, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without failing means doing it perfectly, with no mistakes at all: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lose out, but for country

indicators.note: something out of place or out of order is disarranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of lose rearranged
tho is the informal spelling of though, which can mean but

explanation.surface: A team loses out, but plays on for its country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose out' reads as a phrase meaning to miss out; 'out' alone is the anagram signal. LESOTHO is a small kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a landlocked nation in southern Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Dog lead on wrong, I need assistance!

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of wrong
a cry of someone needing assistance is help!

explanation.surface: A dog owner, having put the lead on wrong, cries out for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a puppy, a young dog, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Old drink for commercial trader

parts.note: ex- means former or old
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: An old drink once favoured by a merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is a dark British beer, a forerunner of stout.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter is a business that sells goods abroad, which makes it a commercial trader.

clue.text: Fractious, able to cut long hair for punishment

parts.note: someone fractious is short-tempered, or short with people
a sharp blade is able to cut
a shock of hair is a thick, long mass of it

explanation.surface: A cross barber, scissors ready, cuts a youth's long hair as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: A short sharp shock is a British phrase for a brief, harsh punishment, famously used of youth detention.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a quick and severe penalty, so it works as a kind of punishment.

clue.text: Land has supported you, humble servant

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
Oman is a land, a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A landowner's estate has kept you on as a modest servant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that supports another sits underneath it. 'Land' tempts as the definition, as yeomen held land, but it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman was historically an attendant or servant in a noble household, a role of lowly rank.

clue.text: Potato destroyed, don't spill the beans, mother!

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
sh! is a call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: A child, having ruined the potato, begs mother not to tell anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first, but the wordplay pieces come in reverse clue order: mother, then the hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is potato pounded to a pulp, so it is potato whose shape has been crushed out of existence.

clue.text: State where name is not false

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A US state where someone's name is not genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Boxing weight lower than others in the end, feel the heat

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of others
welterweight is a boxing weight class

explanation.surface: A boxer, lighter than rivals, sweats it out in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'lower than' puts the boxing weight underneath the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to suffer from oppressive heat, which is what feeling the heat means literally.

clue.text: Man, say, in solver erasing every other letter

indicators.note: removing every second letter leaves the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

parts.note: the odd-placed letters of in solver

explanation.surface: A man in a puzzle solver's role, rubbing out alternate letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, a British island in the Irish Sea; 'say' shows it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of an isle.

clue.text: Obvious, it's said

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one remark that something is obvious, but the clue holds two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced means strongly noticeable, as in a pronounced limp, and also uttered, the past participle of pronounce.

clue.text: Torpor first up, originally nursed

indicators.note: something nursed is held close in the arms, so the letters are cradled inside the words before

parts.note: the letters run across these three words, from the end of the first to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Lethargy came first, and it was tended with care from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursed' looks like part of the story but signals the hiding: the three words before it hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state of near-unconsciousness, a close synonym of torpor or sluggishness.

clue.text: Irritable where intervention of second ref backfired, poor substitute

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: testy means easily irritated

indicators.note: something that backfires goes the wrong way, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: VAR, the video assistant referee in football, is a second referee who reviews decisions

explanation.surface: A football referee gets grumpy when the video review backfires, calling it a poor substitute for real refereeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The video assistant referee in football is known by its initials, the second ref who reviews the on-field decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation or mockery, something that is a poor substitute for the real thing.

clue.text: Particular birthday where fit hero has become wobbly, tummy initially held in

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
something held in sits inside something else, so a letter goes within

parts.note: the letters of fit hero rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of tummy

explanation.surface: A once-fit hero reaches a milestone birthday, wobbly now, holding his tummy in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortieth is a notable birthday that marks turning forty, so it is one particular birthday.

clue.text: Penne and roti put in a blender? Michelin-starred restaurant wouldn't have it!

indicators.note: a blender churns its contents into a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of penne and roti

explanation.surface: Pasta and flatbread blitzed together: no fine-dining kitchen would serve that.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a top restaurant cooks from fresh, so it would have no need for a gadget that opens canned food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener is a kitchen tool for canned food, the kind of shortcut a high-end chef would never use.

clue.text: Giant ostensibly gigantic, really enormous for starters

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning of a meal, so only opening letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A giant seems gigantic, and is indeed enormous, from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, so the two words name the same creature.

clue.text: More petite, the girls dancing about

indicators.note: dancers move around freely, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the girls

explanation.surface: Slender girls flit about the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighter means slimmer or smaller in build, a comparative synonym of more petite.

clue.text: Wheel speeds reversed

indicators.note: turning something back to front means the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: to nip is to go quickly, so speeds is nips

explanation.surface: A wheel goes backwards at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round rapidly, as birds wheel overhead, which is to spin.

clue.text: Invited guest turning company of two into a crowd?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a companion brought along by someone invited

definitions.text: turning company of two into a crowd
definitions.meaning: second, cryptic meaning: adding a single person to a pair

explanation.walkthrough: It plays on the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd': a pair with one added makes three.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus-one is the extra guest an invitee may bring, and adding one to two literally makes three.

clue.text: Free rent: seemingly embarrassed about that

indicators.note: one thing placed about another surrounds it, so a word goes around the other

parts.note: an embarrassed person looks red in the face
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A tenant blushes on being offered free rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free rent' reads as a single phrase, but 'Free' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means set free, as a prisoner is, so it matches the adjective or past participle.

clue.text: Moving this person up, one involved in rigging of vote

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves

indicators.note: being involved in something puts it inside, so a letter goes within others
a rigged vote has been tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of vote rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A politician is moved up the list after joining in rigging the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter, so ME, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means stirring the feelings, which is the sense of moving in a moving speech.

clue.text: Prime Minister nailed up, quit!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for Prime Minister
to ace something is to nail it, do it perfectly

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister is pinned down and told to resign.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, a synonym of quit as a verb meaning depart.

clue.text: Push on drink for squash!

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to press is to push

explanation.surface: A barman pushes a soft drink, squash, on a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'on' puts the first piece after the second. Squash is a British fruit cordial diluted with water.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress is to crush or put down, as a revolt is squashed, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Primate, VIP and famous, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a nob is a person of rank or importance
big, as in a big name, means famous

explanation.surface: A famous ape, star of the zoo, glances over its shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbon is a small tree-dwelling ape, one kind of primate.

clue.text: Tree, a piece of cake to climb

indicators.note: climbing is going upwards, so in a down entry the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: a slab is a thick piece of cake

explanation.surface: Climbing a tree is a piece of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' wants to mean easy; here it is literal, a slab.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree known for its very light wood.

clue.text: Boxing division attributed to a fight, not straightforward

parts.note: a boxing match is divided into rounds
taken as written
a bout is a fight

explanation.surface: A round in boxing is credited to a fight that was not a clean contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundabout means indirect or circuitous, the opposite of straightforward.

clue.text: Meat from lower back cut from buffalo, indigestible!

indicators.note: a piece cut from something is a slice of it, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters sit across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A lower-back cut of buffalo meat proves hard to digest.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is the cut of meat taken from either side of an animal's backbone, near the lower back.

clue.text: Hairy beast bald, it's rumoured

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: bald means bare, which is said like the animal

explanation.surface: Gossip says a hairy beast has gone bald.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear is a large shaggy-coated animal, so it fits a hairy beast.

clue.text: Game endured, giving nothing away

parts.note: poker is a card game
to face something is to endure or confront it

explanation.surface: A card player endures the game without betraying a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker-faced means expressionless, showing no emotion, so a poker-faced person reveals nothing.
